h1: The 6 Best Countertop Dishwashers Under $500 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six countertop dishwashers under $500, covering no-hookup tanks, place settings, wash programs, noise and Energy Star status.
summary: The COMFEE' with a 1.32 gallon built-in tank is the best countertop dishwasher under $500, needing no plumbing, with a 162 degree wash and air-dry. The Energy Star COMFEE' adds eight programs, the EUHOMY is rated at 40dB, the NOVETE offers tank or hose, and two AIRMSEN models serve narrow counters and simple setups.
intro: Countertop dishwashers promise a rental kitchen the one appliance it cannot have. The catch is water. Either you pour it in by hand from a built-in tank, or you screw an adapter onto the faucet and run a drain hose to the sink. Capacity and cycle counts are secondary to that choice, because a dishwasher that does not suit your plumbing is a very expensive drying rack.

Six models were ranked from their titles and specs, and all land in the $200 to $500 bucket, so price does little to separate them. We compared hookup method, place settings, wash programs, noise and efficiency labels, and kept to what each listing claims. Several listings give thin detail, which counts against them because a spec you cannot check is a spec you cannot rely on.

products.name: COMFEE' Portable Mini Dishwasher Countertop with 1.32Gal Built-in Water Tank for Apartments & RVs, No Hookup Needed, 6 Programs, 360° Dual Spray, 162℉ High-Temp & Air-Dry Function
products.verdict: No plumbing, a hot wash and an air-dry cycle.
products.description:
The 1.32 gallon COMFEE' tank model wins because it removes the biggest obstacle to owning one. A built-in tank means no faucet adapter and no plumbing, so a renter, an RV owner or a student can plug in and wash. Six programs, 360 degree dual spray arms and a 162 degree high-temp cycle with air-dry make it a complete wash rather than a rinse, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Hot water helps lift grease and finishes the job on glassware, and air-dry saves hand-towel work. The EUHOMY below is quieter on paper but lists neither feature.

Buy it for apartments, RVs and any kitchen without a drain. The caveat is routine: you fill the tank by hand each cycle, and a small tank limits what a load can use, so large households will find themselves refilling often.

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Dishwasher, Energy Star Portable Dishwasher, 6 Place Settings & 8 Washing Programs, Speed, Baby-Care, ECO & Glass, Dish Washer for Dorm, RV & Apartment, Black
products.verdict: Eight wash programs and Energy Star certification.
products.description:
The Energy Star COMFEE' is the program-variety pick. It holds six place settings, offers eight washing programs including Speed, Baby-Care, ECO and Glass, carries Energy Star certification, and comes in black. Eight programs let you match cycle to load, and the Glass setting is a practical extra when you wash delicate pieces.

It ranks second because its program range is the widest here, but the listing describes no built-in tank, so it probably needs a faucet connection. That is the trade against the tank COMFEE': more choice, less independence.

Choose it for a dorm or apartment with a sink faucet that accepts an adapter. The caveat is hookup: if you cannot attach to a faucet, the no-plumbing models above and below are the safer buy, and the listing offers fewer details on water supply to confirm.
products.idealFor: Dorms and apartments with a faucet.
products.skipIf: You cannot connect to a faucet.

products.name: EUHOMY 6 Programs Countertop Dishwasher Portable, 40dB, 360° Coverage
products.verdict: Rated at 40dB for kitchens close to living spaces.
products.description:
The EUHOMY makes quiet its selling point. It lists six wash programs, a 40dB rated noise level, 360 degree spray coverage and a countertop no-hookup design, in the $200 to $500 bucket. A low decibel rating matters in a studio, where the dishwasher runs a few feet from the couch or the bed.

It ranks third because quiet is the point and little else is listed: it does not mention the hot wash or air-dry features that the top COMFEE' includes. Dishes may need a towel at the end.

Buy it for open-plan living where noise is the main objection to running a dishwasher in the evening. The caveat is features: with no air-dry or high-temp cycle listed, you give up the sanitizing option, so skip it if a hot sanitizing wash matters to you.
products.skipIf: You want a hot sanitizing wash.

products.name: NOVETE Portable Countertop Dishwashers, Compact Dishwashers with 5L Built-in Water Tank & Inlet Hose, 5 Washing Programs, Baby Care, Air-Dry Function and LED Light for Small Apartments
products.verdict: Tank or hose, with a dedicated baby-care cycle.
products.description:
NOVETE offers a choice of water source. It combines a 5L built-in tank with an optional inlet hose, five washing programs including a dedicated Baby Care cycle, air-dry and an LED indicator light. Being able to switch between a tank and a hose lets the same unit move from a rental to a kitchen with a faucet.

It sits fourth because five programs is the fewest in this ranking, and the 5L tank is smaller than the COMFEE' 1.32 gallon tank, so it needs more refills when you use it as a tank model. The Baby Care cycle is the standout.

It suits parents sterilizing bottles. Expect to refill often if you use the tank, and consider the hose if you can connect it. The $200 to $500 price matches the larger-tank COMFEE', so the choice depends on whether bottle care or tank size matters more.

products.name: AIRMSEN Large Slim Countertop Dishwasher | Built-in Water Tank
products.verdict: More interior space in a narrower footprint.
products.description:
The AIRMSEN Large Slim promises more interior space in a narrower body. It has a built-in water tank and a countertop portable design, in the $200 to $500 bucket. Counter width is the limit in many kitchens, and a slimmer unit that still claims capacity is useful in a galley layout.

It ranks fifth because its listing gives no program count, noise rating or place-setting number, so the capacity advantage is unquantified. The COMFEE' models above document their numbers, which is what a buyer needs to compare.

Choose it if counter width is your constraint. The caveat is guesswork: confirm the exact capacity and program list on the product page first, and be prepared to return it if the interior is smaller than you assumed. A promise of larger interior is not a figure.

products.name: AIRMSEN Portable Countertop Dishwasher, No Hookup Needed
products.verdict: A basic no-hookup unit with little detail in the listing.
products.description:
The basic AIRMSEN is a no-hookup unit with a built-in tank and a countertop portable form, in the $200 to $500 bucket. The appeal is simplicity: you fill the tank, load it and run it, with no hose and no faucet adapter to buy.

It trails the group because its listing gives no wash programs, noise level or capacity, while the COMFEE' and EUHOMY listings document theirs. At the same price, that missing detail leaves it a gamble.

It suits buyers who want to keep things simple and do not compare features closely. Compare the product page against rivals before purchase, and treat this as the choice only if the better-documented tank models are out of stock. The caveat is plain: you are buying an unknown cycle list at a known price.

whatMatters.detail: A built-in tank means you pour water in by hand, while a hose model attaches to your faucet. Tanks suit renters but need refilling every run. Check the title for tank volume, such as 1.32 gallons or 5L, or for an inlet hose, and decide whether your sink accepts an adapter or whether you can carry water to the counter.

Six place settings is about a day of dishes for one or two people, so bigger households run it twice. Look for the number in the title, and check what a place setting includes, because plates, bowls and glasses fit differently in a small rack. Pots and large pans often will not fit at all, so plan to hand wash those.

A high-temp cycle of 162 degrees Fahrenheit helps break down grease and sanitize. Not every model lists one, and the tank COMFEE' is the only one here that states the figure. Look for temperature in the spec bullets, and note whether air-dry follows the cycle, since otherwise dishes leave wet and need a towel.

A 40dB rating suggests a quiet machine, important in a studio where it runs near you. Many listings omit noise entirely. Search for dB in the title or bullets, and remember the number is a manufacturer's rating, so treat it as a guide rather than a guarantee, and check whether it applies to every cycle.

These units take a large block of counter. Measure width, depth and the clearance needed to open the door, then compare the product dimensions to your space. A slim body like the AIRMSEN Large Slim helps, but leave room behind for the hose or the power cord, and check that your outlet is close.

faq.a: Some use a built-in tank you fill by hand, like the tank COMFEE' and EUHOMY. Others connect to a faucet with an adapter, like the Energy Star COMFEE' probably does. Check which suits your kitchen and your sink before you order, since this decides everything else.
Ignoring counter space. Measure the unit and the door clearance first, because these dishwashers are bulky, and a tank model also needs space beside it for pouring water in without spilling.

It signals lower water and power use per cycle, which helps if you run it often. The Energy Star COMFEE' carries the label, but the tank COMFEE' wins on installation ease. Energy savings matter less if you run it rarely.

faq.q: How do I set up a tank model?
faq.a: Fill the tank, load dishes, choose a program and run. On the COMFEE' tank model you repeat the fill every cycle, so keep a jug nearby and check the fill line each time.

Clean the filter regularly and run a cleaning cycle to avoid odor. Leave the door ajar after use so the interior can dry, and wipe the seal. Empty any leftover tank water if you will not use it for days.

Large pots often do not fit six place settings. Hand wash them, and use the dishwasher for plates, bowls, cups and glasses where the compact interior works well. Scrape food off first so the filter does not clog.

finalTake: Pick the COMFEE' tank model if you rent or live in an RV, the Energy Star COMFEE' if you have a faucet to connect, and the EUHOMY for a noise-sensitive studio. The NOVETE suits parents washing bottles. Choose an AIRMSEN only after confirming capacity and cycles on the product page.
